'''Konstantinos Papaioannou''' (Greek: Κωνσταντίνος Παπαϊωάννου; 1899 – 6 October 1979)<ref>[http://www.tvkosmos.gr/ Έλληνες τέκτονες ακαδημαϊκοί (Greek academics)]</ref> was a Greek physicist, mathematician, and professor of mechanics at the [[University of Athens]].

==Biography==
He was born in Athens in 1899. He completed secondary school in Athens and then studied at the [[National Technical University of Athens]]. He graduated there in 1919 with a degree from the School of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering. He continued his studies at the University of Athens, where he obtained a degree in mathematics and then a doctorate in mathematics. He was appointed a professor of the University of Athens and became a member of the [[Academy of Athens (modern)|Academy of Athens]].

Papaioannou was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1928 in Bologna, in 1932 in Zurich,<ref>{{cite book|author=Papaïoannou, C. P.|chapter=Sur le mouvement d'une figure plane dans son plan|pages=288–290|volume=2|title=Verhandlungen des Internationalen Mathematiker-Kongresses: Zürich 1932|year=1933}}</ref> and in 1936 in Oslo.<ref>{{cite book|author=Papaioannou, C. P.|chapter=Sur les courbes ayant le même axe anharmonique|title=Comptes rendus du Congrès international des mathématiciens: Oslo, 1936|volume=2|pages=147–149|year=1937}}</ref> He died on October 6, 1979, the same day that [[Anastasios Orlandos]] died.<ref>Νέα Εστία, issue 1256, p. 1521.</ref><ref>Μακεδονία (the newspaper ''Macedonia''), 9 October 1979, p. 15.</ref>

Papaionnou was the (unofficial) referee for the famous 154-page doctoral thesis of [[Christos Papakyriakopoulos]] and had the mathematical ability to immediately foresee Papakyriakopoulos's successful research career.<ref>{{cite web|author=Rassias, Themistocles M.|authorlink=Themistocles M. Rassias|title=The Greek Mathematical Society|website=European Mathematical Society (newsletter) September 2004|pages=34–35|url=http://www.emis.de/newsletter/current/current14.pdf}}</ref>
